failure_summary.description: The answers selected a candidate supported by only part of the clue or gave an associated person instead of the specifically requested title.
The answer repeated an expanded version of a spoonerism anecdote instead of giving the intended phrase behind the altered wording.

patch.reasoning: The existing skill already directs the agent to match the exact answer slot, fit every clue constraint, and prefer direct evidence, so the mint and title errors do not call for duplicative rules. The skill does not explicitly cover reversing verbal wordplay to recover an intended phrase; a narrow general rule addresses that gap.

edits.content:
### Intended phrases in verbal wordplay
When a clue gives a distorted or transformed expression (such as a spoonerism) and asks what was meant, reverse the transformation and return the intended phrase. Do not substitute the altered wording, a longer anecdotal quotation, or another example of the same wordplay.
